A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same LAMP work. Their main text, equations, tables, figures and appendices support reliable comparison, including matching retained material across appendix and figure renumbering.

before.justification: V1 reports original interpolation, extrapolation and drag-optimization experiments on DrivAerNet++ and BlendedNet, plus sample-size ablations and human-annotation-based safety validation.

after.justification: V2 retains those original results and adds initialization experiments, direct linearity validation, decoder-extension examples, safety tradeoffs, high-dimensional extrapolation analysis and plate-with-hole experiments.

M1.justification: The original SDF pipeline is retained, but Appendix M introduces a regularized mixing objective with a lambda-weighted squared coefficient norm and a sweep trading parameter accuracy against safety. Appendix L additionally implements weight interpolation using a sphere-deformation point-cloud decoder. These substantively extend the objective and decoder/output representation; the retained benchmark results are not reported as using these extensions.

E1.justification: Beyond the retained car and aircraft coverage, Appendix O adds six-parameter plates with circular through-holes. Appendix N adds joint 23-parameter extrapolation, substantially extending the simultaneous constraint requirements beyond the original one- and four-parameter out-of-dataset tests. The hole study preserves topology rather than testing transitions between topologies.

E2.justification: DNI and AE-LPA retain their membership in the corresponding benchmark comparisons, including the DNI-only comparison in Table 2. The OpenShape versus random-PointNet surrogate comparison is also retained. The new initialization conditions are LAMP ablations, with no additional competing baseline method introduced.

E3.justification: Existing benchmark settings remain unchanged. New evaluation designs include initialization controls on 100 exemplar decoders, linearity comparisons over 10,000 spatial queries, Monte Carlo evaluation of 10,000 joint parameter targets per extrapolation factor, and 13-exemplar plate experiments with ±100% sweeps. Appendix N also introduces normalized-domain validity and volume measurements.

E4.justification: V2 retains the sample-size ablation and human-label safety validation, while adding tests of shared initialization and seed sensitivity, direct weight/output linearity, non-implicit decoding, conflicting-target safety tradeoffs, high-dimensional reachability and hole stability. These substantially expand investigation of the mechanism, robustness and applicability boundaries.

E5.justification: Appendix F newly distinguishes same-seed and random-seed training while retaining shared initialization, but supplies neither the number of seeds nor across-run uncertainty estimates. Appendix N adds Monte Carlo estimation of valid design volume without confidence intervals. These additions do not establish repeated-run validation of the retained benchmarks.

E6.justification: Tables 1–7 retain their values. New Table 8 reports R²/MAE/safe range of 0.773/0.610/304% with random seeds and -37.77/9.16/0% without shared initialization. Additional findings include approximately 0.99 in-distribution linearity, approximately 8,000-fold estimated safe-volume expansion at f=0.5, and qualitative decoder, tradeoff and hole-stability results. These are newly reported experiments, not improved scores under the original settings.

T1.justification: The assumptions and proofs in Section 3 and Appendices A–C are unchanged. Appendix N adds the mathematical definition VolRatio(f)=(1+f)^23 Valid(f), with the expanded-hypercube volume reasoning. Appendix K supplies empirical support for the existing linearity assumption, not a new proof.

C1.justification: The abstract, introductory contribution list and substantive conclusion retain the same claims about data-efficient parameter control, extrapolation, safety and performance-guided optimization. The new appendix evidence and extensions are not incorporated as revised headline contributions.

C2.justification: V2 newly explains failure from incompatible targets and the accuracy–safety tradeoff in Appendix M, permits application-dependent safety thresholds in Appendix I, and discusses broader decoder applicability in Appendix L. The new limitations section largely consolidates existing topology and local-linearity qualifications, while explicitly adding conflicting requirements as a failure condition.

D1.justification: The added appendices document sphere-template overfitting followed by fine-tuning, parameter normalization to [-1,1], the sampling and validity-filtering workflow, and the plate geometry's six controls. These provide technical information for reproducing the extensions, but no code access information or comprehensive training specifications are added.

R1.justification: Section 2 removes references to MaskedGen, Gen-LDM and CAD2Shape, and uses the retained LION work for the conditional-diffusion discussion. Positioning relative to HyperDiffusion, latent control and model merging remains stable. DeepCAD bibliographic corrections and consolidation of duplicate LION references are not treated as newly introduced research.

P1.justification: V2 adds a standalone Limitations and Future Work section and expands the appendix organization while retaining most main-text prose and ordering. It also fixes the DrivAerNet++ table references from Tables 5/6 to Tables 1/2 and cleans up citation and bibliography wording. The scientific additions do not constitute extensive rewriting of the existing narrative.

P2.justification: New Table 8 and Figures 12 and 22–26 add initialization comparisons, a linearity scatter plot, a decoder example, an accuracy–safety tradeoff, validity/volume curves and hole-geometry sweeps. These substantially expand the visual evidence. All original figures and tables are retained, with some resizing, reflow and subsequent renumbering.

improvement.justification: V2 improves scrutiny of shared initialization and local linearity through Table 8 and Figure 22, and clarifies infeasible targets and safety tradeoffs in Section 5 and Appendix M. These strengthen validation and practical interpretation relative to v1. The broader decoder/topology evidence remains illustrative, and the volume analysis relies on the existing empirical safety proxy; the formal proofs remain unchanged. The net quality gain is positive but limited.
